about: The prayer recalls Peter Celestine’s elevation to the supreme pontificate and his preference for humility. It asks that his example may lead the community to esteem worldly things lightly and attain the rewards promised to the humble.

seg.tr: God, You raised blessed Peter Celestine to the summit of the supreme pontificate and taught him to value humility above that dignity. Graciously grant that, by his example, we may be worthy to despise all worldly things and happily attain the rewards promised to the humble. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who lives and reigns with You in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, forever and ever.

a.g: to the summit of the supreme pontificate
taught him to put humility before it
to happily attain the rewards promised to the humble
who lives and reigns with You
in the unity of the Holy Spirit

ex.w005: The prayer names Peter Celestine, the pope whose dignity and humility are recalled together.
ex.w009: The summit is the height of the supreme pontificate to which God raised Peter.
ex.w012: “It” points back to the pontifical dignity. Peter is the learner whom God taught to place humility above that dignity.
ex.w015: Placing the dignity after humility means esteeming humility more highly. The prayer recalls what God taught Peter.
ex.w027: The humble are the people to whom the rewards are promised.
ex.w030: The requested arrival is a happy and successful attainment of the promised rewards.
ex.w031: “We may be worthy” governs both despising worldly things and attaining the rewards. The two infinitives depend on this final petition.
ex.w048: The word “God” refers to the Son, who lives and reigns with the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit.

nt.w012: The pronoun can also be read as Peter, the learner, with the dignity left understood as what he was to place after humility.
